notices.short_title: CPM Services in Connection with Real Estate Advisory and Tenant Representative Consulting
notices.description:
This solicitation is to obtain services in connection with Real Estate Advisory and Tenant Representative Consulting. The SCA anticipates awarding up to 2 contracts to firms that are prequalified by the SCA at the time of contract award. To assist you with your request, the following is a brief summary of services that will be required:

General Information/Brief Summary:

The firms selected under this RFP will provide the SCA with services in connection with assist in the site identification process, the negotiation of new leases and lease renewals, if necessary, and the purchase of new school construction sites, among various other duties arising out of, or related to, such services.
notices.plain: The School Construction Authority is seeking proposals from up to two prequalified firms to provide real estate advisory and tenant representative consulting, including help identifying school sites, negotiating leases and purchasing new school construction sites, with responses due Oct. 15, 2026.

notices.short_title: COMPASS NAQ
notices.description: Pursuant to Section 3-04(b)(2)(i)(A) of the New York City Procurement Policy Board (PPB) Rules, the Department of Youth and Community Development (DYCD) requests approval to enter into a noncompetitive Negotiated Acquisition with the seven (8) providers to provide programming at 12 middle school locations listed in Attachment A. This procurement maintains critical, uninterrupted Comprehensive After-School System (COMPASS) programming across eleven (12) NYC public schools. These specific school sites were not awarded a contract under the recently concluded competitive solicitation, COMPASS Programs in Public Schools RFP (EPIN: 26026P0003). However, the eleven providers selected for this Negotiated Acquisition are the incumbent contractors at these exact schools. They possess proven track records of satisfactory performance, have built deep roots within their respective school communities, and are uniquely positioned to prevent a lapse in critical student services.
notices.plain: The Department of Youth and Community Development awarded Casita Maria Inc. a $315,900 negotiated contract to keep after-school programming running at middle schools whose sites were not covered by a recent competitive solicitation.

notices.short_title: DYCD Online Negotiated Acquisition Extension
notices.description: Fiscal Year 2027 two (2) year Non-Competitive Negotiated Acquisition Extension for DYCD Online. CBOs use DYCD Online to help accurately report program data to DYCD. ExpandED Schools Inc, provide essential capacity building services to CBO in order to help them acquire the necessary proficiency to utilize DYCD online. CBOs use DYCD Online to help accurately report program data to DYCD. ExpandED Schools develop and facilitate in-person and virtual training sessions on various aspects of DYCD Participants Tracking System (PTS), and DYCD Evaluation Monitoring System (EMS) for staff from DYCD funded Community Based Organizations (CBOs), and DYCD staff. They provide users of PTS and EMS systems with email and phone support, create new user guides and videos as needed, and update existing user guides and videos when PTS and EMS systems are modified and complete and submit monthly, quarterly, and year-end reports on training and support services that were provided, and impact of those services.
notices.plain: The Department of Youth and Community Development awarded Expanded Schools Inc an $886,000 two-year extension, negotiated without open competition, to train community-based organizations and agency staff to use its DYCD Online data-reporting systems.

notices.short_title: Dining Out NYC Public Hearings
notices.description:
NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN, PURSUANT TO LAW, that the following proposed revocable consent has been scheduled for a public hearing by the New York City Department of Transportation. A draft copy of the revocable consent agreement(s) may be obtained at no cost by submitting a request at diningoutnyc.info/requestcopy

The public hearing will be held remotely via Zoom, commencing on October 29th, 2026, at 11:00 am, in the matter of a proposed revocable consent authorizing the following:

  1. ARIARI NYC LLC to maintain, operate, and use a year-round roadway cafe for a term of four years adjacent to 119 1st Avenue in the Borough of Manhattan.

  2. COZY CORNER CORP to maintain, operate and use a sidewalk cafe for a term of four years adjacent to 60-01 70 Avenue in the Borough of Queens.

To join the hearing enter the following URL link into your browsers address bar: zoom.us/j/91467302621 Meeting ID: 914 6730 2621

To join the hearing only by phone, use the following information to connect: Phone: +1-929-205-6099 Meeting ID: 914 6730 2621
notices.plain: The Department of Transportation will hold a remote public hearing on Oct. 29, 2026, at 11 a.m. on proposed four-year revocable consents letting ARIARI NYC LLC run a year-round roadway cafe next to 119 1st Avenue in Manhattan and COZY CORNER CORP run a sidewalk cafe next to 60-01 70 Avenue in Queens.

notices.short_title: Alternative Enforcement Program (AEP) - 5-Year Review - Notice of Intent to Request the Release of Funds - Updated
notices.description:
COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG)

ALTERNATIVE ENFORCEMENT PROGRAM (AEP) 5-YEAR REVIEW - 2026

NOTICE OF INTENT TO REQUEST RELEASE OF FUNDS (NOI RROF)

             

REQUEST FOR RELEASE OF FUNDS

On or about October 19, 2026, the City of New York (the City) anticipates submitting a request to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) for the release of $51,780,000 of Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) funds authorized under Title I of the Housing and Community Development Act of 1974, (PL 93-383), as amended, to undertake the Citys Alternative Enforcement Program citywide, for a period of five years.

The Alternative Enforcement Program (AEP) is intended to address the serious physical deterioration of the most distressed buildings in New York City. Through AEP, the NYC Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) can order the property owner to repair or replace building systems as well as to address violations. Using criteria set forth in the City's Administrative Code, HPD annually designates…
notices.plain: The Office of Management and Budget gave notice that New York City plans to ask the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development on or about Oct. 19, 2026, to release $51,780,000 in Community Development Block Grant funds for the city's Alternative Enforcement Program over five years.

notices.plain: The Taxi and Limousine Commission extended its Accessible Taxi Loan Assistance Program (ATLAS) pilot for a second year, starting Sept. 29, 2026, so it can reach its maximum of 100 participants.
